chapters.chapter_summary: Arjuna, overwhelmed by sorrow and delusion at the sight of his kinsmen arrayed for battle on the field of Kurukshetra, sinks down in his chariot and refuses to fight.
Krishna speaks of the immortality of the soul, the nature of dharma, and introduces Nishkama Karma — selfless action — and the 'Sthitaprajna' (person of steady wisdom).
Krishna explains the necessity of action and the importance of performing one's duties without attachment to results, introducing Yajna as a cosmic mechanism.

chapters.name_meaning: The Yoga of Wisdom, Action & Renunciation
chapters.chapter_summary: Krishna reveals that He has taught this eternal wisdom in past ages and explains the divine nature of His incarnations, describing different types of sacrifices.

chapters.name_meaning: The Yoga of Renunciation of Action
chapters.chapter_summary: Krishna reconciles renunciation and selfless action, showing they lead to the same goal. A sage acts without being bound by karma.
Krishna describes Dhyana Yoga (meditation), proper posture, and the characteristics of a perfected yogi. He addresses the fate of a yogi who does not complete the path.
Krishna reveals His divine nature as the source of all creation, His eight material energies, and speaks of four types of devotees who approach Him.

chapters.name_meaning: The Yoga of the Imperishable Absolute
chapters.chapter_summary: Krishna explains the process of death and describes the paths of light and darkness, assuring that those who remember Him at death attain Him.

chapters.name_meaning: The Yoga of Royal Knowledge & Royal Secret
chapters.chapter_summary: Krishna reveals the most confidential knowledge — the science of devotion — describing how the universe exists in Him yet He transcends it.
Krishna enumerates His divine manifestations, explaining that everything beautiful or powerful in creation is a spark of His splendor.

chapters.name_meaning: The Yoga of the Vision of the Cosmic Form
chapters.chapter_summary: At Arjuna's request, Krishna reveals His awe-inspiring Cosmic Form (Vishvarupa). Arjuna is overwhelmed with wonder and fear.
Krishna declares that direct devotion to His personal form is superior to meditating on the impersonal Absolute, and describes the qualities of His most beloved devotees.

chapters.name_meaning: The Yoga of the Field & the Knower of the Field
chapters.chapter_summary: Krishna explains the distinction between the body (field) and the soul (knower of the field), describing the nature of knowledge and the qualities leading to liberation.

chapters.name_meaning: The Yoga of the Three Modes of Nature
chapters.chapter_summary: Krishna explains the three modes of nature (sattva, rajas, tamas) and how they bind the soul, describing how to transcend them through devotional service.

chapters.name_meaning: The Yoga of the Supreme Person
chapters.chapter_summary: Using the metaphor of the inverted Ashvattha tree, Krishna describes material existence and reveals Himself as the Supreme Person, Purushottama.

chapters.name_meaning: The Yoga of the Divine & Demoniac Natures
chapters.chapter_summary: Krishna describes the divine and demoniac natures, emphasizing that those with divine qualities are destined for liberation.

chapters.name_meaning: The Yoga of the Threefold Faith
chapters.chapter_summary: Krishna explains how the three modes influence faith, food, sacrifices, austerities, and charity, introducing the sacred formula 'Om Tat Sat'.

chapters.name_meaning: The Yoga of Liberation through Renunciation
chapters.chapter_summary: Krishna summarizes the entire Gita, explaining tyaga (renunciation), the role of the three gunas, and concludes with the most secret teaching — full surrender to Him.
